title: Convergent Clifford-valued Hermite-semigroup kernel series and equality on the explicit Laguerre-monogenic basis for kappa=0, c>-1, dimension m>=2 and Re omega>0
author: Hendrik De Bie; Bent Orsted; Petr Somberg; Vladimir Soucek
source_title: The Clifford Deformation of the Hermite Semigroup
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs separate reproducing kernels for monogenic and vector-monogenic sectors and matches their radial Bessel-Laguerre integrals with the deformed oscillator eigenvalues. It then controls all angular Gegenbauer and growing-order Bessel contributions by a gamma-denominator estimate to obtain the convergent kernel series, beyond formal spectral exponentiation or a classical Mehler substitution.

proof_review.note: Read full Theorem6.2, the new Clifford Funk-Hecke/reproducing-kernel construction Lemma5.1/Proposition5.1, spectral matching in6.1 and complete series bound. Earlier Laguerre-monogenic basis and osp(1|2) action are explicitly published background from[7]; exact basis, weighted Hilbert space and parameters are supplied Sections3-4. Selection keeps kappa=0 as the standing restriction after4.4, realc>-1,m>=2,Re omega>0, and h(r)=r^(1-(1+mc)/(1+c)). The conclusion is convergence of the stated A,B series and agreement on that basis. m=2 uses the explicit lambda->0 Gegenbauer convention Remark5.2. Known Bessel/Laguerre integral and AppendixA bounds are named background. No distributional boundary-limit theorem6.3, Fourier variants, unitarity-only or uncertainty corollary counted.

statement_scope: Full Theorem6.2 for the undeformed Dunkl case kappa=0,dimensionm>=2,c>-1,Re omega>0. The original Clifford-valued A,B Bessel-Gegenbauer series converge and its weighted integral transform agrees with the specified spectral semigroup on every basis vector phi_(t,l,index). No claim of pointwise integration for every L2 representative or boundary Re omega=0 is added.
